newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia sees export earnings decline in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia sees export earnings decline in 1996/97.

text.p: Ethiopian export earnings will marginally fall in 1996/97 compared to the previous year because of a drop in global prices of its main products, Trade and Industry Minister Kassahun Ayele said on Monday.
He put earnings in 1996/97 at $421.05 million versus $440.4 million in 1995/96 and blamed global prices for the decline.

"The fall in the export earnings could be attributed to a drop in price of coffee, livestock, leather products -- Ethiopia's main export items in the world market," Kassahun told a gathering celebrating "Export Day" in Addis Ababa.

Coffee is Ethiopia's main cash crop and accounts for up to 60 percent of its foreign exchange earnings. Ethiopia exported 102,000 tonnes of coffee in 1995/96 and earned $279.5 million, compared to $330.9 million from sales of only 78,420 tonnes in 1994/95.
Ethiopia plans to export 108,000 tonnes of coffee in 1996/97. It has already exported 48,300 tonnes during the first seven months of the current fiscal year (July/June) and earned $120 million.

Kassahun said that of the total $421.05 million expected from exports in 1996/97, some $42.1 million was from livestock and meat exports, $63.2 million from leather products, $279.5 million from coffee and the rest from oil seeds, gold and horticultural products.
Kassahun said the share of the private sector in Ethiopia's export trade had increased steadily in recent years.

Private exporters accounted for 51 percent of coffee, 25 percent of hides and skin, 89 percent of cereals and oil seeds and 79 percent of livestock exports in 1996/97 compared to just under 19 percent in 1990, he said.
